name: Monitor investment compliance
summary: Every business day a three-person compliance team checks the overnight run of the compliance engine, which tests each pool, client account and external manager account against the restrictions coded from client IMAs, investment policies, pool guidelines and pension investment rules. Analysts triage a few dozen alerts, spend much of the morning chasing alerts caused by bad security reference data, answer pre-trade override requests and investigate the few possible real breaches with portfolio managers or external managers. Confirmed breaches are classified by the chief compliance officer, logged, reported to the client where required and tracked until cured; stale feeds, weekend gaps and external manager response times stretch the elapsed time.

baseline.org_archetype: A provincial not-for-profit asset manager of about $79 billion with pools, segregated client accounts and about 120 external manager mandates.
baseline.notes: Rule-based compliance engine inside the order management and book of record platform, breach register and exception log in spreadsheets, email for escalation.

unit_of_work: one business day's compliance run with its alerts
trigger: The investment book of record closes the business day and the overnight compliance batch runs on the day's positions and trades.
end_state: Every alert has a disposition, pre-trade overrides are decided, confirmed breaches are classified, logged, notified and tracked to cure, and the daily checklist is signed.

evidence.note: Canadian business days per month, as the organisation file's demand driver.

About 6.4 hours of analyst time per business day at 21 days a month is about 1.0 FTE, plus rule maintenance outside the run. Loaded cost from the organisation file, above the Job Bank NOC 11109 median ($34.62 an hour in Toronto, 2023-2024) after variable pay and the 1.35 loading.
Breach review and weekly oversight; the CCO reports to the board on the compliance system (osc_mgr_2017).
Stands in for the internal portfolio managers who explain and fix breaches in their portfolios.
Organisation file role not listed on this process; corrects security reference data behind false alerts.

roles.title: Client relationship manager (lead for one or two clients)

evidence.note: Organisation file role not listed on this process; tells the client about breaches its policy requires to be reported promptly.

systems.name: Order management, pre-trade compliance and investment book of record platform (vendor software as a service)
Custodian portal (custody, accounting records, net asset value reports, cash and corporate action notices)
Market data terminals and vendor feeds (prices, indices, reference data)
Code of conduct, personal trading pre-clearance and attestation system
Document management system and virtual data rooms
Email, video calls and collaboration suite

steps.name: Load end-of-day positions, trades, prices and reference data
steps.description: After the investment book of record closes the day, the compliance engine in the order management platform loads positions and trades for every pool, client and external manager account, custodian holdings for external mandates, prices, exchange rates and security reference data.

next.condition: next day is a business day

evidence.note: End-of-day compliance checks on positions at market close are standard engine functions; timing tier C.

steps.name: Results wait over the weekend or holiday
steps.description: When the run falls before a weekend or holiday, the overnight results and alerts sit until the next business day because the compliance team does not work weekends.

evidence.note: About one run in five precedes a weekend or holiday.

steps.name: Run the overnight post-trade compliance rules
steps.description: The engine tests every coded rule (client IMA and policy restrictions, pool guidelines, mandate guidelines, concentration and voting share limits, leverage and derivative limits) against the day's holdings and produces the alert list.

control.basis: OSC exemption order for the model manager: compliance system preventing investments that contravene IMA restrictions

evidence.note: The model manager must prevent contraventions of IMA restrictions (osc_mgr_2017); Schedule III 10% and 30% limits apply to pension clients (pbsr_sch3).

steps.name: Check the run is complete and the feeds are current
steps.description: In the morning the compliance analyst checks that the run finished for every account, that custodian and external manager holdings files arrived for the right date and that prices are not stale, before trusting the alerts.

evidence.note: Holdings spread across several systems and sub-advisers make complete data a known problem; the 15% rate is tier C.

steps.name: Chase the missing feed and rerun
steps.description: The analyst asks investment data management or the custodian for the missing or stale holdings or price file, waits for the reload and reruns the affected accounts.

evidence.note: Common practice; times tier C.

steps.name: Triage the day's alerts
steps.description: The analyst works down the alert list, typically a few dozen items, separating known and approved exceptions, passive drifts within cure periods, alerts caused by bad reference data and possible real breaches, and records a first disposition for each.

error.defect_description: A real breach is dismissed as a data issue.

evidence.note: The organisation file says false alerts from bad reference data take much of the time; alert counts and times are tier C.

steps.name: Investigate data-driven false alerts
steps.description: For each suspect alert the analyst looks up the security in the market data terminal and the security master, finds the wrong issuer link, sector, country, rating or asset type behind it and raises a correction request to investment data management.

evidence.note: Reference data errors drive false positives in rule engines; times tier C.

steps.name: Correct the security reference data
steps.description: An investment data analyst checks the request against vendor data, corrects the security master record (issuer hierarchy, classification, rating or identifiers) with a second check and confirms the fix to compliance.

error.defect_description: Correction introduces a new classification error.

evidence.note: Security master maintenance sits with investment data management in the organisation file; times tier C.

steps.name: Rerun the affected rules
steps.description: The compliance engine reruns the rules for the accounts holding the corrected securities so that false alerts clear and any remaining alerts reflect real positions.

evidence.note: Standard engine function; timing tier C.

steps.name: Review ownership and regulatory threshold report
steps.description: The analyst reviews the aggregate holdings report across all pools and client accounts for issuers near the voting share limit or securities law reporting thresholds, and for related party and restricted list hits.

control.basis: Pension Benefits Standards Regulations Schedule III (30% rule, related party rules) as incorporated in client policies

next.condition: threshold crossed or about to be crossed

evidence.note: 30% voting share limit and related party rules for pension clients; the 3% daily rate is tier C.

steps.name: Notify legal of a threshold crossing
steps.description: The analyst confirms the aggregate position, the date the threshold was crossed and the accounts involved, and sends it to legal for the ownership or regulatory filing and to the portfolio managers to stop further buying.

control.basis: Securities law ownership reporting thresholds in Canada and abroad

evidence.note: Ownership filings are handled in the regulatory filings process; times tier C.

steps.name: Answer pre-trade warnings and override requests
steps.description: During the trading day the analyst reviews soft pre-trade warnings that portfolio managers or traders ask to override, checks the rule and the reason given and approves or rejects the override, escalating hard blocks to the chief compliance officer.

control.basis: Compliance approval of pre-trade override requests, independent of the portfolio manager

next.condition: a possible real breach remains after triage

evidence.note: Alerts let compliance supervisors approve or reject blocked trades; volumes and times tier C.

steps.name: Investigate the possible breach
steps.description: The analyst confirms the holding with custodian or manager records, rereads the guideline or IMA wording, checks whether the rule is coded correctly and whether the position arose from a trade (active) or from market movement or a corporate action (passive).

error.defect_description: Breach misclassified as passive or within cure period.

next.condition: not a breach: coding, timing or interpretation
breach in an external manager account

evidence.note: Active versus passive classification is common practice; rates tier C.

steps.name: Portfolio manager explains the breach and proposes the fix
steps.description: The internal portfolio manager confirms how the position arose and proposes a fix and timing, such as selling the excess, closing a derivative or waiting for a cure period, and states whether the client lost money.

evidence.note: The process map lists the portfolio manager; pm_public_equities stands in for fixed income, credit and total portfolio managers.

steps.name: Notify the external manager and request its explanation
steps.description: The analyst emails the external manager's compliance officer with the position, the guideline breached and the date, copies the mandate's portfolio manager and manager research, and asks for the cause, the fix and any compensation proposal.

evidence.note: Sub-advisers must be monitored; follow-up of the manager by the portfolio manager is in ext-manager-monitoring. Times tier C.

steps.name: External manager confirms the cause and the fix
steps.description: The manager's compliance team confirms or disputes the breach, explains the cause and the corrective trades and says whether it will compensate the account for any loss.

evidence.note: Manager response times are tier C.

steps.name: Chief compliance officer reviews and classifies the breach
steps.description: The chief compliance officer reviews the assessment and fix, classifies the breach as material or not under the compliance policy, approves the remediation and cure date and decides who must be told: the client, the CIO and the board committee.

control.basis: OSC exemption order for the model manager: chief compliance officer oversight of the compliance system

evidence.note: A CCO with direct board access oversees the compliance system and reports annually to the board; review times tier C.

steps.name: Log the breach and notify the teams
steps.description: The analyst records the breach, cause, remediation, cure date and loss in the breach register, and sends the compliance exception to the portfolio manager or manager research, client reporting and the investment team.

error.defect_description: Breach logged with the wrong client or cure date.

control.basis: Breach register as evidence for the SOC 1 controls report and board compliance reporting

evidence.note: Books and records must show compliance; client notification share is tier C.

steps.name: Tell the client about the breach
steps.description: The client relationship manager calls and writes to the client's investment staff about the breach, its cause, the fix and any compensation, as the client's policy or IMA requires for material breaches.

control.basis: Client IMA and investment policy breach reporting terms

evidence.note: Prompt client notice of material breaches is common in IMAs; the model manager's terms are not public.

steps.name: Close the day's run
steps.description: The analyst finishes dispositions for every alert with a comment, updates the exception log, saves the evidence and signs the daily compliance checklist.

control.basis: Daily evidence of post-trade compliance review tested in the SOC 1 Type 2 report

evidence.note: Evidence of control operation supports the model manager's SOC 1 reports; times tier C.

steps.name: Confirm the breach is cured
steps.description: In the following runs the analyst checks that the corrective trades settled and the alert cleared by the agreed cure date, and records the cure in the breach register.

next.condition: not cured by the agreed date

evidence.note: Cure tracking is common practice; times and rates tier C.

steps.name: Escalate an uncured breach
steps.description: The chief compliance officer escalates a breach that is not cured on time to the general counsel and the chief investment officer, agrees a new deadline or forced action, and notes it for the board committee report.

evidence.note: CCO direct access to the board; escalation path tier C.

steps.name: Weekly review of dispositions and overrides
steps.description: Once a week the chief compliance officer samples the alert dispositions and pre-trade overrides, reviews open breaches and repeat false alerts, and asks for rule or data fixes.

control.basis: Compliance policy: supervisory review of alert dispositions and overrides

next.condition: day and weekly review signed off

evidence.note: Supervisory review is common practice; weekly frequency tier C.

exceptions.name: Missing or stale feed
exceptions.description: Custodian or external manager holdings or prices arrive late or for the wrong date and the run is repeated for the affected accounts.

exceptions.name: Breach in an internal portfolio
exceptions.description: A possible breach is confirmed in an internally managed portfolio and the portfolio manager proposes the fix.

exceptions.name: Breach in an external manager account
exceptions.description: The external manager is notified, explains and corrects the breach; the portfolio manager follows up in ext-manager-monitoring.

exceptions.name: Uncured breach escalated
exceptions.description: The breach is not cured by the agreed date and the CCO escalates to the general counsel and CIO.

exceptions.name: Ownership threshold crossing
exceptions.description: Aggregate holdings near a voting share limit or reporting threshold go to legal for filing.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from close of business to the signed daily checklist (longer on breach days)
benchmarks.population: Daily post-trade compliance runs at a Canadian public asset manager (author's estimate)

evidence.note: End-of-day checks run overnight and are reviewed the next morning; weekends and breach follow-up set the 90th percentile.

benchmarks.unit: share of plan market value in one person or group
benchmarks.population: Pension plans under the federal investment rules, applied by Ontario pension clients

benchmarks.unit: share of votes to elect directors
benchmarks.population: Pension plans under the federal investment rules
The insurance client pension fund policy, 2019

evidence.note: Organisation file demand driver.

pain_points.description: False alerts from wrong issuer links, classifications and ratings take much of the morning and need a data fix and rerun.

evidence.note: Stated in the organisation file's process description.

pain_points.description: External manager holdings come from custodian files a day late and managers take a day or more to answer breach notices.

evidence.note: Holdings across sub-advisers and systems lack a single view.

pain_points.description: The breach register and exception log are spreadsheets, so cure tracking and board reporting are assembled by hand.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for the period.

pain_points.description: Derivative and leverage limits are hard to code and test, so they generate more warnings and manual checks.

sources.title: The model manager, Commission and Director decisions (exemptions for the model manager and its investment pools)
sources.supports: Board-approved policies must establish the model manager's compliance system; a chief compliance officer with direct board access presents annual compliance reports to the board; policies must prevent investments by a pool or for a member that contravene the restrictions set out in the IMAs; books and records must show compliance; sub-advisers must be vetted and monitored; personal trading and insider trading restrictions.

sources.title: Pension Benefits Standards Regulations, 1985 (SOR/87-19), Schedule III Permitted Investments
sources.publisher: Justice Laws Website, Government of Canada
sources.supports: Section 9: no loan or investment in one person, associated persons or affiliated corporations if 10% or more of the plan's total market value is already, or would as a result be, invested in them; section 11: no investment in securities carrying more than 30% of the votes to elect directors, with exemptions for real estate, resource and investment corporations.

sources.title: Statement of Investment Policies and Procedures for the Public Service Pension Plan (approved 3 December 2025)
sources.supports: Investments must comply with the Income Tax Act, the Pension Benefits Act and the Federal Investment Rules in Schedule III; the 10% concentration test applies at the time of the loan or investment; recourse and non-recourse debt limited to 10% of fund value; related party transactions only as Schedule III permits; leverage within the strategic asset allocation and the model manager's leverage policy.

sources.title: The insurance client Pension Fund Statement of Investment Policies and Procedures, effective January 1, 2019
sources.supports: Pooled funds must meet the 10% rule (section 9) and 30% rule (section 11) of Schedule III; related party transactions only if nominal (no more than 3% of fund value) or immaterial; derivatives permitted for stated purposes under a derivatives policy; securities lending under an approved policy.

sources.title: The model manager 2021 Annual Report
sources.supports: Investment risk management monitors compliance with client mandates and performs limit monitoring; the model manager gave clients a clean SOC 1 Type I report on the design of its controls and planned a Type II report for 2022.

sources.title: The model manager 2022 Annual Report
sources.supports: Inaugural SOC 1 Type 2 report with a clean opinion that controls were designed and operated effectively from 1 October 2021 to 30 September 2022.

sources.title: Trading and investment compliance solutions
sources.supports: Compliance constraints checked at order modelling and trade entry in the order management system, end-of-day checks validating firm and portfolio positions at market close with an audit trail, automated alerts letting compliance supervisors approve or reject blocked trades, and curated regulatory reference data.

sources.title: Buy side assesses pre-trade compliance
sources.supports: Derivatives, leverage and long-short strategies strain pre-trade compliance engines; pension funds and funds of funds often lack a holistic view of holdings spread across several systems and sub-advisers; gaps push firms to add compliance staff.

sources.title: Wages: Financial Compliance Officer (NOC 11109) in the Toronto Region
sources.supports: Toronto region hourly wages low $23.00, median $34.62, high $66.46 (reference period 2023-2024).

assumptions: One case is one business day's run across all pools, client accounts and external mandates; touch minutes are the team's total work on that run, not per account.

Coding of rules for new clients, new policies and new mandates is done in client-onboarding-transition, client-ips-asset-mix-review and ext-manager-onboarding; those triggers appear here as the inputs that change the rule set, with small shares, and the daily trades captured by trade-capture-confirmation trigger the run.

Pre-trade override requests are answered during the trading day while the post-trade alerts are worked; the step is marked concurrent, so the simulated cycle time overstates real elapsed time by up to an hour.

On about 25% of days a possible real breach survives triage; about 70% of those are confirmed, so roughly 3 to 4 breaches a month are logged, mostly passive. These rates are estimates for about 250 accounts and 120 mandates.
pm_public_equities stands in for all internal portfolio managers; follow-up of external managers by the portfolio manager is counted in ext-manager-monitoring, not here.

The simulator adds every role's hands-on minutes in sequence (about 7 hours a day), while in practice two or three analysts split the alert list; the simulated median of about 1.3 days therefore sits above the 1.0 day estimate, and the 90th percentile reflects weekends and breach follow-up.
Daily investment risk limits and client asset mix ranges are monitored in daily-risk-limit-monitoring, not here.
data_analyst and client_relationship_manager are organisation file roles that the process map does not list for this process; they appear for reference data fixes and client notification.
The pension client policy cited is the December 2025 version; the Schedule III rules it incorporates and the insurance client 2019 policy show the same restrictions applied in the reference period.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file (Job Bank Toronto wages deflated to 2021, variable pay and a 1.35 loading).
Web searching ran out while this workflow was researched, so sources were limited to pages fetched by address and saved copies; alert volumes and rates are tier C.
